interest: Reveals prewar chemical technology transfers to Mitsui and diplomatic refutation of Robert Ripley's 'Made in Sweden' match myth.
overview: This file documents Japanese chemical and manufacturing industries during the 1930s, focusing on industrial technology transfers, corporate market disruptions, and international trade issues. Central records detail du Pont's controversial licensing of synthetic ammonia and hydrogen contact conversion processes to Mitsui amid State Department concerns regarding Japanese military preparedness. The file also covers the shutdown of the Swedish-controlled Daido Match Company, an official diplomatic investigation debunking Robert Ripley's claim that Japan named a town 'Sweden' to mislabel matches, a ten-year Chilean-Japanese iodine export cartel, and agricultural petitions for fertilizer regulation.
